overview: FCC first recommends deferring SCAP's proposed Japan-U.S. rate change pending its own 1947-48 international-rate investigation, then considers a Bermuda Agreement-style Japan-Korea-Okinawa rate framework, before a SCAP directive finally equalizes outbound Japanese radiotelegraph charges with increased U.S./Hawaii-to-Japan rates.

people.name: Francis Colt de Wolf
people.role: Chief, Telecommunications Division, U.S. Department of State

people.name: Walter A. Radius
people.role: Director, Office of Transport and Communications, U.S. Department of State

subfiles.title: FCC letter recommending deferral of SCAP telegraph-rate request
subfiles.from: T. J. Slowie, Secretary, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Francis Colt de Wolf, Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC recommends deferring action on SCAP's proposed change in telegraph rates between Japan and the United States pending a broader investigation of international communications charges.
subfiles.summary: Slowie recommends postponing SCAP's proposed Japan-U.S. telegraph rate change pending the FCC's new investigation into international communications charges, with hearings starting in April.

subfiles.title: FCC acknowledgment concerning rates for Japan, Korea, and Okinawa
subfiles.from: Paul A. Walker, Acting Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Walter A. Radius, Director, Office of Transport and Communications, Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC acknowledges receipt of a SCAP despatch on telegraph rates and relates it to negotiations over country-to-country rates based on the Bermuda Agreement model.
subfiles.summary: Walker acknowledges SCAP's despatch on Japan-Korea-Okinawa telegraph rates, noting it answers FCC's Bermuda Agreement-style country-to-country rate discussions, still under Commission consideration.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 105 on equalization of radiotelegraph rates
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser's office transmits a SCAP directive revising radiotelegraph rates from Japan to the United States and Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 105 forwards SCAPIN 1228/8 (Feb. 1948), notifying Japan of revised radiotelegraph charges matching increased U.S./Hawaii-to-Japan rates.

interest: Shows 1947-48 U.S.-SCAP-FCC negotiations equalizing Japan-U.S. radiotelegraph rates, modeled partly on the Bermuda Agreement.
